justification: Removes five invented values that were shown to users as planning controls for any property inside a Transport Oriented Development area. The Transport Oriented Development Sites Map (ArcGIS MapServer/3) carries 9,562 features and its fields are exactly OBJECTID, EPI_NAME, PUBLISHED_DATE, COMMENCED_DATE, AMENDMENT, MAP_NAME, LAY_CLASS, LABEL, PRECINCT, SHAPE. The code read 'Maximum FSR'/'Max FSR'/'FSR', 'Maximum Height'/'Max Height'/'HEIGHT', 'Legislative Clause'/'Clause', 'EPI Name' and 'Precinct Name' -- none of which exist on that layer -- so the ternary and || fallbacks were not cover for an occasional gap, they were the ONLY code path and fired for every mapped area. Users saw 'Max FSR 2.5:1' and 'Max Height 24m' as this property's controls, cited to 'Clause 4.4'. Critical because 24m is wrong on the law (s155(2) caps a residential flat building at 22m) and 'Clause 4.4' is the ordinary LEP floor-space clause, nothing to do with transport oriented development, whose standard is s155. Cross-review raised three findings on the first push and both distinct defects were REAL and are fixed. (1) HIGH: the panel stated s155's figures without s155(5), which provides the section does not apply to the extent another chapter or instrument permits a greater height or floor space ratio — so 2.5:1 read as a ceiling on a property whose LEP permits more. s155(5) was quoted in this change's own code comment and omitted from the text users read: the same error as stating a necessary condition as a sufficient one, which #1228 fixed on the in-fill card hours earlier. (2) MEDIUM: this change had repointed the SEE parking control's clause at 'Chapter 5', which is the TOD height and FSR chapter, while the requirement beside it concerns parking under s24/42/68/74 — a citation made worse, not better, by the edit. Both are now pinned by assertions and forced red. A THIRD review round raised two more, both real and both introduced by this change. (3) LOW: the s155(5) regression assertion scanned RAW source, so the comment quoting the subsection beside the JSX could satisfy it after the visible paragraph was deleted. Forcing that deletion did fail — but only because the comment says 'maximum building height' and the rendered text says 'maximum height', one word's luck. This is the identical flaw already fixed in __tests__/compliance/sepp-parking-cards-match-law.test.tsx hours earlier, rewritten from scratch in a new file. read() now strips comments. (4) MEDIUM: 'LEP controls remain in force until rezoning is gazetted' was carried from the ACCELERATED precinct panel, which does await a rezoning, into the MAPPED TOD panel, where s155 already operates — inverting it, and inviting a reader to treat a lower LEP limit as governing. Replaced with interaction wording; the accelerated panel keeps the sentence, and a test asserts both. A FOURTH round raised one more, real and demonstrated before fixing. (5) LOW: the s155(5) assertions still matched the whole comment-stripped file, so the caveat could sit anywhere in it. Forced: deleting the visible caveat from the assessment page's TOD panel and moving the same words into an unused constant left ALL 21 assertions green. Both assertions are now scoped to their panel's own region, and that mutation fails. Sol's suggested fix — render both components with React Testing Library — is DECLINED as disproportionate for a text assertion: StateLevelControls takes a large prop surface and AssessmentPage is a full page with hooks and fetches, and the sibling citation suite (sepp-parking-cards-match-law.test.tsx) already establishes source-scoping as the pattern here. Partial accept: the hole is closed, by scoping rather than by rendering. A FIFTH round raised one more, real: s155(5) has TWO limbs — 'a provision of another chapter of this policy OR another environmental planning instrument' — and operates 'to the extent', not absolutely. The assessment page named only the second limb and said 'where' rather than 'to the extent', so a greater standard elsewhere in the Housing SEPP itself would have read as not displacing s155. Both panels now mirror both limbs and the partial-operation qualifier, and dropping either fails.

pre_impl.existing_data: The live ArcGIS layer, read directly rather than inferred. Its metadata endpoint (MapServer/3?f=json) lists 10 fields and none is FSR, height or clause. A sample query returned real attributes: PRECINCT 'KOGARAH', EPI_NAME 'State Environmental Planning Policy (Housing) 2021', AMENDMENT 'Newcastle Local Environmental Plan (Housing) (Map Amendment No 1)'. returnCountOnly reports 9,562 features. Section 155 of SEPP (Housing) 2021 was read verbatim from the whole-instrument PDF in force for 11 September 2026.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: Four assumptions broke, and the order they broke in is the point. (1) First claim: the page shows invented numbers 'when the Portal omits them' -- wrong, the omission is unconditional. (2) Retraction: 2.5 and 24 are the real statutory figures so nothing is invented -- also wrong. s155(2) sets 22m for a residential flat building and only s155(3) sets 24m, for seniors or shop top housing, so 24 is wrong for the commonest TOD case. (3) The defect would be observable by testing addresses -- wrong: five real addresses were tested, including three near TOD stations, and none was inside a TOD area, so sampling could never have settled it. (4) property_reports would show whether todPrecinct had ever been populated -- wrong table, it holds only satellite products (shadow 568, flood 287, bushfire 71, solar 63) and has never held a planning assessment. What settled it was reading the layer's own field list.
pre_impl.external_source_error: The ArcGIS service is the external dependency and it answered: metadata 200 (38,387 bytes), count 200, sample query 200. Separately, legislation.nsw.gov.au rate-limits: after ~8 requests it returned 'Server Busy' for one instrument and a Cloudflare challenge for the next, and legislation_monitor.py already sleeps 5s between requests for this reason. At runtime getTODLayers already wraps both ArcGIS calls in an 8s AbortController and catches to an empty array, so a layer outage yields no todPrecinct rather than a partial one -- that behaviour is unchanged by this PR.
pre_impl.frontend_type: maxFSRBonus, maxHeightBonus and legislativeClause are DELETED from TODPrecinctInfo rather than made optional, so TypeScript fails anyone reinstating a reader. precinctName and seppReference become optional (string | undefined) because the layer can be silent, and amendment is added. tsc --noEmit reports 0 errors across the repo after the change, which is also what proves no consumer was missed: the three that read the deleted fields are all updated.
pre_impl.user_failure_mode: A planner or owner opens a property inside one of the 9,562 TOD areas and reads 'Max FSR 2.5:1' and 'Max Height 24m' under the heading 'TOD Development Standard Bonuses', cited as 'Clause 4.4'. They design to 24m where s155(2) allows 22m for a residential flat building, and go looking for the standard in Clause 4.4, which is about floor space ratio in the LEP and says nothing about TOD. Both failures are silent: the figures render identically to the Portal-sourced height and FSR beside them, which ARE real.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: No new component, route, table or migration. Four existing files change and one test file is added. The TOD branch of extractPlanningConstraints keeps its shape and loses five literals; two render sites lose the tiles that printed them and gain a sentence naming s155 with a link, reusing the SeppCitationLink component #1224 already shipped rather than a new link widget. Applies to every property view on deploy, and only changes what a TOD property shows -- a non-TOD property renders no todPrecinct at all, before or after.

falsifiable_check.fails_when: Any of the five literals returns: the 2.5 FSR, the 24m height, the 'Clause 4.4' citation, the 'TOD Precinct' placeholder, or the 'SEPP (Housing) 2021' guess. Also fails if the reader goes back to a key the layer does not have ('Precinct Name', 'EPI Name' with a space), or if a silent layer yields anything other than undefined. Also: the s155(5) exception dropped from either render site; the text reverting to a claim that s155 'sets' the controls; or the SEE parking citation naming Chapter 5 instead of the development-type parking sections. Also: the s155(5) assertion passing on a comment rather than rendered text; the mapped-TOD panel telling the reader to wait for a rezoning; or the accelerated panel losing that sentence, where it is correct. Also: the s155(5) caveat present anywhere in the file but NOT inside the TOD panel's own region; or either panel region slicing empty, which would make its assertions vacuous. Also: either limb of s155(5) missing from a panel, or 'to the extent' replaced by 'where'.
falsifiable_check.observed_red: Five mutations forced, each restored afterwards (baseline 12 passed). Restoring the 2.5 FSR literal: 3 failed / 9. Restoring the 24m height literal: 3 failed / 9. Restoring 'Clause 4.4': 3 failed / 9. Reading 'Precinct Name' instead of PRECINCT: 1 failed / 11. Reading 'EPI Name' instead of EPI_NAME: 1 failed / 11. Restored: 12 passed. The suite's fixture is a real feature from the live layer (OBJECTID 258648, Kogarah), not an invented one, so a mismatch between the code's expectations and the layer's actual shape fails here rather than in production. Three further mutations after the cross-review fixes. Dropping the s155(5) caveat: 1 failed / 16 of 17. Reverting to 'are set by section 155': 1 failed / 16. Restoring 'Chapter 5' in the SEE parking citation: 2 failed / 15. Restored: 17 passed. Eight mutations across both pushes, all caught. Third round: deleting the VISIBLE s155(5) paragraph while leaving its comment fails 1 of 21 (and still fails after read() was changed to strip comments, which is the point — it now fails by design rather than by a wording coincidence). Restoring 'LEP controls remain in force until rezoning is gazetted' in the mapped panel fails 2 of 21. Eleven mutations across three rounds, all caught. Fourth round: deleting the visible caveat from the assessment page's panel and parking the words in an unused constant passed 21 of 21 BEFORE the scoping fix and fails 1 of 21 after. Twelve mutations across four rounds, all caught. Fifth round: dropping the 'another chapter of SEPP (Housing) 2021' limb fails 1 of 21; replacing 'to the extent' with 'where' fails 1 of 21. Fourteen mutations across five rounds, all caught. The rounds converged — HIGH, then MEDIUM, then LOW, then LOW, then wording accuracy — and three of the five found the defect in a test written in this branch.
falsifiable_check.measured: 21 tests pass in the new suite, each s155(5) assertion scoped to its panel region with a non-empty-slice guard. Full frontend suite 117 suites / 1,631 tests passed (116 / 1,610 on origin/main). npx tsc --noEmit: 0 errors. One further self-inflicted defect was caught during the third fix and is guarded: the new panel-scoping slice used 'Accelerated TOD Precinct' as its end marker, a string that also appears EARLIER in the file, so the slice was empty and two assertions were vacuous. Offsets were measured (39,749 vs 17,461), the marker repointed at the accelerated panel's own sentence, and a test now asserts the slice is non-empty.

functions.name: NSWPlanningPortalService.extractPlanningConstraints — TOD branch
functions.input: a PlanningLayer whose layerName getTODLayers set to 'Transport Oriented Development Sites Map', carrying the layer's own attributes
functions.output: todPrecinct with inTODArea, and precinctName / seppReference / amendment only where the layer supplied them
functions.if_none: every field other than inTODArea is undefined, so a caller renders nothing. Previously a silent layer produced 2.5, 24, 'Clause 4.4', 'TOD Precinct' and 'SEPP (Housing) 2021'.

functions.name: assessment page — TOD panel
functions.input: selectedProperty.constraints.todPrecinct, the object extractPlanningConstraints built for this address, carrying inTODArea plus whatever the map supplied
functions.output: the precinct name, the distance to the station where known, and a sentence naming s155 with a link to it
functions.if_none: the two tiles that printed FSR and height are gone entirely; an unnamed precinct reads 'Precinct not named on the Transport Oriented Development Sites Map' rather than a placeholder

functions.name: StateLevelControls — TOD standards block
functions.input: propertyData.constraints.todPrecinct, passed down as a prop from the assessment page's property fetch, read only for its inTODArea flag now
functions.output: s155's three figures stated WITH the development types they attach to, plus a SeppCitationLink to sec.155
functions.if_none: the block renders only when inTODArea is true; it no longer depends on two fields that were always present because they were literals

values.guard_at: the TypeScript interface, which no longer declares it, and the test asserting it is undefined
values.if_missing: correct by construction. s155 makes the height depend on the development type, which an address cannot supply, so no single value can be right. The card names both figures and the types they apply to instead.

values.nullable: yes — the layer may omit it
values.guard_at: precinctName?: string, and the assessment page's ?? branch
values.if_missing: the panel says the precinct is not named on the map, rather than labelling every area 'TOD Precinct'

break_it.scenario: A property sits inside one of the 9,562 TOD areas and the user designs to the height shown.
break_it.what_happens: They now read that s155 sets 22m for a residential flat building and 24m for seniors or shop top housing, and can open s155. Before, they read a flat 'Max Height 24m' for any proposal.
break_it.how: The literal is deleted from the interface, so it cannot be rendered. Forced: restoring it fails 3 of 12.
break_it.repro: cd frontend-nextjs && npx jest __tests__/lib/tod-no-fabricated-standards.test.ts -t 'states NO floor space ratio or height'

break_it.scenario: The ArcGIS layer changes its field names, e.g. PRECINCT becomes PRECINCT_NAME.
break_it.what_happens: precinctName and seppReference become undefined and the panel says the precinct is not named. It does NOT fall back to a literal, which is what hid the original defect for however long it stood.
break_it.how: Every reader is `|| undefined`, and the 'map feature with nothing in it' suite asserts an empty attribute bag yields undefined on all five fields and contains none of the old literals.
break_it.repro: cd frontend-nextjs && npx jest __tests__/lib/tod-no-fabricated-standards.test.ts -t 'never produces the literals the old code used'

break_it.scenario: Someone reinstates a hardcoded standard because the card looks empty without one.
break_it.what_happens: tsc fails — the three fields are deleted from TODPrecinctInfo, not optional — and the jest suite fails on the literal.
break_it.how: Two independent gates, type and test. Forced on all three deleted fields.

break_it.scenario: The same shape of defect exists elsewhere in this file.
break_it.what_happens: NOT addressed. extractPlanningConstraints has many other branches with || literals (e.g. treeCanopy's year: '2019' and source string), and this PR changes only the TOD branch.
break_it.how: Deliberately scoped. The TOD branch was measured against its layer's real schema; the others were not, and guessing at them would repeat the error this PR fixes. A sweep of every branch against its own layer metadata is the follow-up, and belongs with DQ-133/134 as a gate rather than a one-off read.

break_it.scenario: Nobody has ever loaded a TOD property, so none of this reached a user.
break_it.what_happens: Possible and unmeasured. The layer holds 9,562 features so the areas exist, but whether a session hit one cannot be read from here: property_reports holds satellite products only.
break_it.how: Affects urgency, not correctness. The defect is deterministic for anyone who does load one, and the fix is safe regardless.

break_it.scenario: A mapped TOD property's own LEP permits a greater height or floor space ratio than s155's figures.
break_it.what_happens: Both render sites now state s155(5) — that the section does not apply to the extent another chapter or instrument permits more — and point the reader at the LEP tab's controls for the same property. Before, 2.5:1 read as the ceiling.
break_it.how: Cross-review HIGH/correctness, verdict real, fixed. The wording also changed from 's155 sets' to 's155 identifies standards', which is the section's own framing and survives subsection (5). Forced: dropping the caveat fails 1 of 17; reverting the wording fails 1 of 17.
break_it.repro: cd frontend-nextjs && npx jest __tests__/lib/tod-no-fabricated-standards.test.ts -t 'discloses the subsection (5) exception'

break_it.scenario: A reader follows the SEE report's parking control citation.
break_it.what_happens: It names sections 24, 42, 68 and 74 — the development-type parking provisions the requirement itself refers to. An intermediate version of this change said 'Chapter 5', the TOD height and FSR chapter, which says nothing about parking.
break_it.how: Cross-review MEDIUM/correctness, verdict real, fixed. Forced: restoring 'Chapter 5' fails 2 of 17.
break_it.repro: cd frontend-nextjs && npx jest __tests__/lib/tod-no-fabricated-standards.test.ts -t 'does not cite Chapter 5'

break_it.scenario: A later edit deletes the visible s155(5) paragraph but leaves the comment that quotes it.
break_it.what_happens: The suite fails, because read() strips comments before matching. The first version of these assertions scanned raw source and survived on a one-word difference between the comment and the rendered text.
break_it.how: Cross-review LOW/correctness, verdict real, fixed. Forced after the fix: deleting the visible paragraph while keeping the comment fails 1 of 21.
break_it.repro: cd frontend-nextjs && npx jest __tests__/lib/tod-no-fabricated-standards.test.ts -t 'discloses the subsection (5) exception'

break_it.scenario: A reader of a mapped TOD property is told the LEP governs until a rezoning.
break_it.what_happens: The mapped panel now says to read the LEP and SEPP controls together, and that which applies depends on the proposal and s155 including subsection (5). The accelerated panel, where a rezoning IS pending, keeps its original sentence.
break_it.how: Cross-review MEDIUM/correctness, verdict real, fixed. The assertions are scoped to the mapped panel's own region of the file, and a separate test asserts the accelerated panel retains the sentence. Forced: restoring it in the mapped panel fails 2 of 21.
break_it.repro: cd frontend-nextjs && npx jest __tests__/lib/tod-no-fabricated-standards.test.ts -t 'does not claim LEP controls hold until rezoning'

break_it.scenario: The s155(5) caveat is deleted from a TOD panel but the same words survive elsewhere in the file.
break_it.what_happens: The suite fails. Each assertion reads only the region between its panel's heading and the next element, with a guard that the region is non-empty, so a dead branch, another component or a constant cannot satisfy it.
break_it.how: Cross-review LOW/silent-failure, verdict real, demonstrated then fixed. Before: deleting the visible caveat and moving the words to an unused constant passed 21 of 21. After: fails 1 of 21.
break_it.repro: cd frontend-nextjs && npx jest __tests__/lib/tod-no-fabricated-standards.test.ts -t 'discloses the subsection (5) exception inside the TOD panel itself'

break_it.scenario: Another chapter of SEPP (Housing) 2021 itself permits a greater height or FSR for the proposal.
break_it.what_happens: Both panels state that s155 does not apply to the extent another chapter of the Housing SEPP, or another instrument, permits more. An earlier assessment-page draft named only 'another instrument', which would have read as though a greater standard inside the same SEPP left s155 controlling.
break_it.how: Cross-review, verdict real, fixed. Both limbs and the 'to the extent' qualifier are asserted inside each panel's own region. Forced: dropping the chapter limb fails 1 of 21; replacing 'to the extent' with 'where' fails 1 of 21.
break_it.repro: cd frontend-nextjs && npx jest __tests__/lib/tod-no-fabricated-standards.test.ts -t 'discloses the subsection (5) exception inside the TOD panel itself'

post_merge.manual_verify: Yes -- load a property inside a TOD area on the preview and confirm the panel names s155, discloses subsection (5), shows no FSR or height figure, and does not say LEP controls hold until a rezoning. I could not do this: five real addresses were tested and none was inside a TOD area, and we hold no TOD geometry to find one from. The layer reports 9,562 features, so such properties exist.
